correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity gives the exact necessary and sufficient equation p^(ell^2)+1=q(p+p^ell-1). For p>2, modulo D=p+p^ell-1 the left side has nonzero residue 1-(p-1)^ell with absolute value below D, contradiction. For p=2 the quotient is integral because ell is odd and equals Phi_(2 ell^2)(2); primality of this quotient is exactly the remaining condition. The converse follows by substitution. Exact packaged checks corroborate all critical finite examples.

The theorem gives a uniform explanation of that phenomenon for every odd prime-square exponent, rules out all odd base primes, and reduces the full infinite stratum to one natural cyclotomic primality question.
